title: Singapore’s job as ASEAN chair: fixing how the grouping decides
gist: Ahead of Singapore's 2027 ASEAN chair, the author argues ASEAN's real flaw is delegation rather than speed, and proposes using Charter Article 20 for a decision allowing pre-authorised crisis action in 72-hour windows renewed by silence.

insights.claim: Singapore takes the rotating ASEAN chair in 2027, the bloc's 60th anniversary, with a crowded agenda: Community Vision 2045, Timor-Leste's admission, upgraded trade agreements, Myanmar, a failed Thai-Cambodian accord, an unfinished South China Sea code of conduct and a Gulf energy shock.
insights.speaker: Prathap Latchmanan
insights.so_what: Expect a deliverable-heavy but possibly cautious chairmanship.

insights.claim: PM Lawrence Wong's 2027 priorities are a real single market and broader external partnerships, with the ASEAN Power Grid central; Singapore and Thailand (2028 chair) agreed a joint multi-year agenda.
insights.speaker: Prathap Latchmanan
insights.so_what: Two-year continuity improves odds that energy and market integration reforms survive.
insights.locator: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has named

insights.claim: Four member priorities are energy (fuel-sharing under the ASEAN Petroleum Security Agreement is still voluntary), a digital economy agreement due for signing in November, scam centres (51.4% of ISEAS survey respondents named them a main concern), and Myanmar.
insights.speaker: Prathap Latchmanan
insights.so_what: Regional energy security and digital trade are the likely areas of concrete progress.
insights.locator: Members want progress in four areas

insights.claim: ASEAN's crisis problem is delegation: it can mobilise within hours but cannot decide within days; speed was never the issue, authority was.
insights.speaker: Prathap Latchmanan
insights.so_what: Institutional reform of crisis authority is the author's key test of the chairmanship.
insights.quote: Speed was never the issue. Authority was.
insights.locator: My view is that ASEAN’s crisis problem is delegation

insights.claim: Charter Article 20 lets the Summit decide how to decide when consensus fails, and the author proposes one decision with objective triggers, 72-hour release of pre-positioned relief by the Secretary-General and AHA Centre, renewal by silence within 24 hours, pre-signed access templates, and 90-minute crisis rehearsals.
insights.speaker: Prathap Latchmanan
insights.so_what: A rule-based fast-action mechanism would materially change ASEAN's crisis responsiveness if adopted.
insights.locator: The Charter already offers a way through

insights.claim: On Myanmar the author wants Singapore to set dates, such as a verified halt to airstrikes and a named prisoner list agreed with the UN by mid-2027, backed by non-political representation at ministerial meetings if missed, but expects Thailand to resist.
insights.speaker: Prathap Latchmanan
insights.so_what: Myanmar benchmarks risk dilution given Thai preference for re-engagement.
